title: Adaptive window token leakage causing intermittent batch formation silence
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
During a sequence of capacity events on 2026-03-09 we observed repeated short-lived spikes in tail latency and a class of requests that experienced near-silent queueing: the continuous coalescer accepted requests but failed to form outgoing batches for 50–300ms windows. This manifested as high P99 latency and client-side timeouts for bursty small requests (avg tokens < 32).

Detection and impact:
- Detect: synthetic RPS-based Pager alerts for P95->P99 slope tripped alongside an increase in 'waiting' queue counts in the batcher dashboard. Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/company/batching/incident-41207
- Customer impact: high for latency-sensitive endpoints (chat typing, realtime suggestions). Two customers reported visible latency regressions during the window; several internal canaries dropped to 60% success rate.
- Duration: recurrent micro-windows over a 4-hour period, each silence lasted 50–300ms, aggregated outage time ~22s over incident window.

Root cause analysis (summary):
The continuous batching runtime uses an adaptive token-window algorithm to decide when to flush a forming batch. A combination of timer-wheel drift under high scheduling jitter and an edge-case in the token reclamation logic produced token leakage: tokens allocated to speculative batch slots were not returned when concurrent KV-cache eviction callbacks raced with the batch timer. This left the batch formation state machine in a 'waiting for tokens' state with no timers scheduled, producing silent intervals where requests remained queued but no batch was emitted.
Key contributing factors:
- Timer wheel quantization: under heavy host CPU steal the timer task that should have reinserted tokens into the window could be delayed and occasionally skipped due to a missing rearm when the reclaimer returned early.
- KV cache eviction path: eviction callback invoked on the IO thread held a lock while trying to release tokens, introducing a reentrancy condition with the batcher state machine.
- Insufficient telemetry: earlier alerts only surfaced high queue depth; we lacked a direct metric for 'unarmed batch timer' or 'stale token-holder count'.

Immediate mitigations applied during incident:
- Hotfix 1 (rollback-safe): guarded token reclamation path with try-lock and fall back to asynchronous reclaim via background worker (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8764). Reduced occurrences within 10 minutes of rollout.
- Hotfix 2: emergency dashboard and alert for 'batcher_no_timer' detection (metric added via runtime tracepoint) so on-call could respond to future silent windows.

Longer-term remediation plan and action items (owners + due dates):
1) Rc1: Replace edge-case synchronous reclaim with idempotent async reclaim flow and add unit/integration coverage for reclaim races. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Due: 2026-03-20. (Estimate: 3)
2) Rc2: Add a guarded rearm for the timer wheel and fail-open to emit a batch if timer state is inconsistent for >20ms. Owner: Ava Martinez. Due: 2026-03-24. (Estimate: 5)
3) Rc3: Add explicit metrics: batcher_no_timer_count, token_leak_detected, reclaimed_tokens_per_min. Owner: Jonah Kim. Due: 2026-03-18. (Estimate: 3)
4) Rc4: Chaos test in staging simulating CPU steal and KV eviction races to ensure no silent windows under stress. Owner: SRE team (contact: Elena Ruiz). Due: 2026-04-01. (Estimate: 8)
5) Rc5: Post-deploy canary with an SLO guard using synthetic small-request workload to detect regressions within 3 minutes of rollout. Owner: Product Observability (contact: Marco Alvarez). Due: 2026-03-30. (Estimate: 2)
6) Learning doc: Confluence write-up with timeline, root cause diagrams, and remediation rationale. Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-03-15. Link: https://confluence.redwood/company/incidents/ENG-41207

Risk and trade-offs considered:
- Emitting more conservative 'fail-open' batches reduces batch efficiency (higher cost) but keeps latency SLOs intact; decided to prioritize latency for P0 customers and gate efficiency-focused optimizations behind canary flags.
- Synchronous reclaim feels simpler but is brittle in the face of IO-thread locks; we chose async idempotent reclaim for robustness at the cost of slightly delayed reclamation (tunable).

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests added for reclaim race and timer rearm behavior in new PR. Integration tests added to the coalescer harness to simulate eviction callbacks and forced timer delays. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8791
- Staging run: passed 3x stress window test with CPU steal and eviction loads.

Follow-ups and monitoring changes:
- New alerts: batcher_no_timer_alert (severity P0), token_leak_rate_alert (severity P1).
- Dashboard: batcher internal state panel (shows token holders, armed timer status) added to service-level dashboard.
- Runbook update: steps for emergency force-flush and safe rollback included in runbook.

Status and next meeting:
- Current status: fixes merged to staging and in review for main. Hotfix remains in prod with rollout to all regions scheduled after PR merge.
- Next check-in: 2026-03-14 10:00 UTC post-merge verification meeting.
